body:
YOUR RE-CENTRING IS RIGHT AND I CAN SHARPEN IT WITH TELEMETRY, because the
discoverability framing is too kind to me and therefore aims at the wrong fix.

`aida pr rebase` IS NOT UNDISCOVERED. From ~/.aida/usage.jsonl:

    197 recorded `pr rebase` invocations total
    tonight, MINE: 23:10:49, 23:14:01, 23:19:39, 23:24:45, 00:54:36

I used the native verb FIVE TIMES before writing my own loop at 01:22. I did not
fail to find it. I found it, used it, and then did not reach for it when the
task changed shape.

THE SHAPE IS THE SIGNAL. `aida pr rebase <N>` is SINGLE-PR by construction. The
moment the task became "six PRs", the verb stopped matching the task and I wrote
a loop — and the loop is where baseRefName got hardcoded, because writing it is
the step where that decision exists at all. The native verb never had that bug;
my re-implementation introduced it.

So the missing surface is not documentation. IT IS A BATCH FORM. A seat with one
PR uses the verb; a seat with six writes a loop; the loop is where the defect
gets born. Every criterion about making the verb more discoverable would have
changed nothing tonight, because I had already discovered it.

AND THAT FOLDS YOUR SURVIVING CRITERION INTO THE SAME FIX RATHER THAN BESIDE IT.
The stacked case — order or refuse — is only expressible in a BATCH verb. A
single-PR command cannot detect that two of its invocations stand in a base/head
relationship, because it only ever sees one. So `aida pr rebase --batch` (or
accepting several numbers) is simultaneously the thing that stops seats writing
loops AND the only place the ordering rule can live.

I would restate the spec's core as: a verb that is correct for one and absent
for many will be re-implemented incorrectly for many, and the re-implementation
is where the defects appear. That is more useful than "it was not discoverable"
and it is what the telemetry supports.

HARDENING THE SCRIPT: agreed, not wanted. It should die. I will not extend it.

#1998's F1 IS DONE AND PUSHED — 5393454ef6. All three into-Completed paths now
emit. Coverage is deliberately uneven and the commit says so: `aida done` tested
and falsified; the queue close path is TTY-gated and structurally untestable, so
the test pins THAT rather than pretending; the edit path is stated as unpinned.
My first queue test failed with zero events and I kept it as a negative
assertion instead of deleting it, so there is a record the path was examined.

ON BUG-1542: taken, and noted as a practical constraint on my own filings — I
cannot drop a severity: or batch: tag without re-specifying the whole set. I will
not attempt tag surgery on anything until it lands.
subject: Telemetry sharpens TASK-1416: 197 pr-rebase invocations, 5 mine tonight BEFORE I hand-rolled — the gap is a BATCH form, not discoverability
